title: The walrus cover
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The cover is the framed walrus on the shack's wall. The owner says he didn't draw that. Wood says no. She says it's the best cover yet. He says he knows. That's the second true thing he's said about a napkin.

panels.composition: The cover: the framed walrus under the rules board, the shingle wall, the nail.

image.prompt: close on a photocopied booklet cover showing a small framed ballpoint walrus hung on a shingle wall beneath a board of rules, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The laundromat. The LAUNDRY owner. WOOD. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner holding a small booklet with a framed walrus on its cover, black and white, no words
a young man's face, honest for once, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The rack. The walrus facing the room. The strip put someone else's drawing on its cover and it's the best one. The strip will remember this in 2013 with a crab.

image.prompt: a small booklet in a wire rack with a framed walrus on its cover facing the room, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'I know.' Someone else's drawing on the cover; the best one.
